meta.instructions: Manual diagnostic tool -- browses a folder on DCG's real SFTP server (via the Transfer Family connector's StartDirectoryListing API) and shows what's actually there, no waiting on Chi Cao to confirm. Defaults to /From_SCL_TEST; to check a different folder (e.g. /To_SCL_TEST, /From_SCL_PROD), pin data on the trigger with { remoteDirectoryPath: '/To_SCL_TEST' } or edit the StartDirectoryListing node's RemoteDirectoryPath directly. Needs transfer:StartDirectoryListing on the n8n IAM user's policy (see clients/scl-footwear/docs/n8n-aws-iam-policy.json) AND s3:PutObject/GetObject/ListBucket on scl-dcg-sftp-bridge/dcg-listings/* on the CONNECTOR's OWN access role (scl-dcg-transfer-connector-role -- a separate IAM role from the n8n user, used by AWS's backend to actually write the listing output; confirmed live 2026-08-06 that this role was originally scoped only to the dcg/* prefix and needed dcg-listings/* and outbound/* added). If this tool returns NoSuchKey when reading the listing file, check that role first, not the n8n user's policy. After import, re-select credentials: AWS account (both AWS nodes). Parse Listing's output shows fileCount/pathCount/truncated and the full files/paths arrays (filePath, modifiedTimestamp, size per remote file) -- confirmed live 2026-08-06 the real response shape is { files: [...], paths: [...], truncated: bool }, not a bare array. An empty files array means nothing has actually landed in that DCG folder yet.
